transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (CTO, Oakwood), David Ruiz (Platform Eng), Karen Li (Security Manager), Tom Nguyen (DevOps)

Summary: Demo focused on rate limits, quotas and multi-tenant controls. Showed Console config for org vs project keys, quota windows, overflow/fallback policies, and API behavior including rate limit headers. Discussed security and billing separation.

Topics: rate limits; org/project keys; quota scopes; RBAC; SSO/SAML; audit logs; billing segmentation.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Uh quick intro — I'm Maya, AE, and Liam is our SE who will run the demo.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Hey all — I can take you through the Console and then show the API behavior. Mmhmm.
[00:20] Sara Patel: Thanks, Maya. We're short on time — high level, we want to understand how you enforce rate limits across multiple tenants and how we can map those to our org and project structure. Also want to confirm we can keep billing separated by project.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: Great. Quick qualifier — are you planning to use Redwood hosted or dedicated/private?
[00:40] David Ruiz: Likely hosted to start. We may move critical workloads to dedicated later. For hosted we need clear guarantees around per-project quotas and audit logs.
[00:49] Karen Li: And SSO, SAML integration and KMS for key material, we'll need those for compliance.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Totally — we'll cover those. Today we'll demo org level controls, project-level keys, quotas, and the Console pages for RBAC and audit logs, and show the API responses for rate-limited requests.
[01:06] Liam O'Connor: Ok jumping into the Console — top-right you'll see the org settings. Here we create projects under the org, and each project can get its own project key. The org key is higher-level and can enforce org-wide quotas.
[01:20] [01:20] Speaker 1: (some screen delay)
[01:25] Liam O'Connor: Example: we set an org monthly token quota 10M and then per-project soft quotas to split the allocation. If one project spikes, you can configure overflow to route to a fallback model or throttle.
[01:37] Tom Nguyen: How granular can we get — by route or by model? We have some endpoints that are embeddings-heavy and some for chat.
[01:44] Liam O'Connor: You can scope quotas by project and by route (we call them API routes) — so you can give embeddings a different budget. On the API side we expose headers so clients can see remaining tokens and reset windows.
[01:54] Sara Patel: Are rate limits enforced at the token level or request level? We worry about bursty traffic causing tail latency.
[02:01] Liam O'Connor: Good question. Limits are typically token-based but you can also configure request-per-minute limits. The efficient path is to throttle by tokens and use per-route priorities so critical routes get preference. There's also a burst window to allow short spikes.
[02:15] [02:15] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[02:20] Maya Chen: From a billing perspective you can split invoices by project, or aggregate at org level depending on your invoicing needs. That was asked earlier.
[02:29] David Ruiz: For hosted, if a project hits quota, do you return 429s? Or is there a soft denial with queued requests?
[02:36] Liam O'Connor: Default is a 429 with a Retry-After header. But you can set soft-limits where requests are allowed but tagged and billed differently; or set overflow rules to redirect to a cheaper quantized model or fall back to cached responses.
[02:49] Karen Li: Can audit logs show which project key was used and the user who triggered it via SSO? We need traceability for audits.
[02:57] Liam O'Connor: Yes — audit logs include key ID, project ID, actor (if SSO is integrated), timestamp, and action. We keep logs configurable retention; for Private you can set longer retention.
[03:09] Sara Patel: SSO — does Redwood support SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:13] Maya Chen: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. We'll share the SSO guide and SAML cert exchange docs after the call.
[03:21] Tom Nguyen: On enforcement — if we use project keys in our microservices, can we rotate keys without downtime?
[03:27] Liam O'Connor: You can create multiple active keys per project; implement dual-write during rotation. We also support short-lived keys via our Token API for ephemeral service tokens.
[03:36] [03:36] Speaker 3: (brief pause)
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: Now the API demo — I'll make a few requests to show headers. First normal request to the chat endpoint.
[03:47] [03:47] Liam O'Connor: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer PROJECT_KEY_xxx" https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat ... sending.
[03:56] [03:56] Response printed: 200 OK, headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 50000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 49872, X-RateLimit-Reset: 1690700000
[04:06] David Ruiz: That header naming is helpful. Are those token counts or request counts?
[04:09] Liam O'Connor: Those are token counts by default for generation endpoints. For embeddings endpoints we show separate token buckets.
[04:15] Karen Li: If an org reaches its monthly quota, can we set automatic bill-overflow to a paid overage or to stop all requests?
[04:23] Liam O'Connor: Both — you can configure billing overflow to allow overage at a higher unit price or set a hard stop which returns 429s. Most customers pick soft-overflow for non-critical workloads.
[04:33] Sara Patel: Any way to do per-team quotas inside a project? Our teams are mapped inside a single project for now.
[04:39] Liam O'Connor: Projects are the main isolation unit now; for finer isolation you can create more projects or use tags and enforce via routing policies. We also have route-level quotas which can approximate team isolation.
[04:51] [04:51] Speaker 1: (typing)
[04:56] Liam O'Connor: Quick note on enforcement latency — rate limit checks are evaluated at the edge with a centralized quota controller; typical enforcement is sub-50ms extra latency.
[05:07] Tom Nguyen: Ok performance sounds good. For dedicated mode, does enforcement change? Do we run our own controller?
[05:14] Liam O'Connor: In Dedicated we still manage quota policy but the controller can be colocated in your VPC; we provide an HA controller and can expose metrics to Prometheus.
[05:24] David Ruiz: Security: KMS — can Redwood integrate with customer-managed keys?
[05:29] Maya Chen: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key material. For hosted we offer Redwood-managed KMS with export controls and can sign BAA. We'll share the integration notes.
[05:42] [05:42] Speaker 2: (background noise)
[05:47] Liam O'Connor: Now walking through Console: here's the org dashboard showing token consumption by project, heatmaps, and projected overage at current burn rate.
[05:58] Sara Patel: Can we get those metrics to our CloudWatch or Splunk?
[06:02] Liam O'Connor: Yep — we have export connectors and webhooks. For enterprise customers we set up an observability pipeline to forward logs and metrics.
[06:11] Karen Li: On RBAC — can we limit who can create project keys? We need separation between billing admins and devs.
[06:17] Liam O'Connor: Role-based permissions exist: Org Admin, Billing Admin, Project Admin, Developer. You can restrict key creation to Project Admins only.
[06:26] Maya Chen: Quick interjection — typical deployment pattern we see: dev teams get project keys, infra uses org keys for shared utilities, billing team gets org-level billing views.
[06:36] David Ruiz: What about rate limiting for long-running streaming requests? We have streaming transcriptions that hold a connection open.
[06:44] Liam O'Connor: Streaming is metered separately — we track in-flight tokens and also have concurrency limits. You can set concurrent-connection caps per project. If you exceed concurrency, new streams get a 429 or queued depending on config.
[06:58] [06:58] Speaker 3: (laugh)
[07:02] Tom Nguyen: Is there a preview API we can hit to simulate quotas before committing?
[07:07] Liam O'Connor: We provide a sandbox org and can provision a trials org with preconfigured project keys and quotas so you can run traffic. We'll spin that up as a next step.
[07:16] Sara Patel: Ok let's talk edge cases — what happens if a downstream service misbehaves and spikes tokens? Can we throttle a single key without affecting the whole project?
[07:25] Liam O'Connor: Yes — keys are first-class. You can blacklist/soft-throttle individual keys. You can also set per-key rate limits and tie a key to a service account so it's auditable.
[07:36] Karen Li: Are the audit logs tamper-evident? We need integrity guarantees.
[07:41] Liam O'Connor: We can provide append-only logs with cryptographic checksums as part of the enterprise package; for Private deployments you can ship logs to your audit infra. We'll include that in the security pack.
[07:53] [07:53] Speaker 1: (phone beep)
[07:58] Maya Chen: I'll quickly demo the API behavior for hitting a hard quota. Liam will trigger a high-traffic loop.
[08:06] [08:06] Liam O'Connor: Running load now — hitting the project key with 200 rps.
[08:12] [08:12] Console output: multiple 429s returned, headers include Retry-After: 60, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
[08:19] David Ruiz: The Retry-After looks straightforward. Is there a jitter/backoff recommended?
[08:23] Liam O'Connor: Standard exponential backoff + jitter, and honoring Retry-After. Our SDKs built-in will do that automatically.
[08:30] Karen Li: When a project hits quota and overage is enabled, how is billing calculated retroactively? Does the invoice show itemized overage per project key?
[08:39] Maya Chen: Invoices can be itemized per project. Overage shows as a line item with the unit price applied for the overage. We can also configure alerts as you approach thresholds.
[08:49] Sara Patel: Good. Who in Redwood will we work with for SOC2 artifacts and penetration test evidence?
[08:55] Maya Chen: I'll connect you directly to our security team; we'll attach the SOC2 snapshot and standard pen test summary.
[09:01] [09:01] Speaker 2: (note-taking)
[09:07] Liam O'Connor: A couple more things — API keys are scoped; if you present an org key, project scoping rules still apply and requests are attributed to the project specified in the request metadata. We also support project scoping via subdomain if you prefer.
[09:21] Tom Nguyen: Subdomain mapping could simplify routing for us. Do webhooks respect project keys as well?
[09:27] Liam O'Connor: Yes, webhook deliveries include key metadata so you can filter.
[09:31] Sara Patel: Can we configure alerts for unusual token burn rates? We want to be notified before we hit quotas.
[09:36] Liam O'Connor: Alerting is built-in — thresholds on rate of change, absolute consumption, and anomaly detection.
[09:42] [09:42] Speaker 3: (agreement mmhmm)
[09:45] Maya Chen: Quick recap before we run out: we'll send the security pack, spin up a trials org with project keys, and schedule a technical deep dive/load test. Any blockers?
[09:56] David Ruiz: None so far. We'll send our traffic profile.
[10:00] Sara Patel: Timeline — we want to evaluate over the next two weeks and hopefully start a POC in August.
[10:06] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Liam — anything else to show?
[10:10] Liam O'Connor: One last demo: policy-driven fallback. If Project A exceeds quota, route requests to a lower-cost quantized model automatically, so product remains available albeit at lower fidelity.
[10:24] [10:24] Console animation: policy editor open
[10:30] Tom Nguyen: That fallback could be useful for non-critical features. How do we measure quality regression when falling back?
[10:36] Liam O'Connor: We tie fallback events to our Optimize tooling which runs evals on holdout prompts. You can set regression alerts if quality drops beyond a threshold.
[10:47] Karen Li: We need to log fallback events to our SIEM. Is that possible?
[10:52] Liam O'Connor: Yes — events are exported via webhook or SIEM connector.
[10:56] [10:56] Speaker 1: (typing)
[11:02] Maya Chen: Ok let's go into a quick q&a — please raise anything we missed.
[11:07] Sara Patel: How easy is it to migrate keys if we reorganize projects later?
[11:12] Liam O'Connor: We provide a migration API to reassign keys and re-map historical billing to new project IDs for accounting. It does require a short maintenance window for large remaps.
[11:23] David Ruiz: For the load test — do you provide tooling or should we run it from our side?
[11:28] Liam O'Connor: We can provide a load harness and also run a co-led test with your infra team.
[11:33] Tom Nguyen: A performance note — you mentioned the centralized quota controller. Is it a single point of failure?
[11:38] Liam O'Connor: No — it's HA with local caches at the edge for short windows; if the controller is unreachable, the local edge will continue honoring last-known quotas for a configurable grace period.
[11:52] [11:52] Speaker 2: (laugh)
[11:56] Maya Chen: Last administrative question — pricing model for overage: is it flat per-token or tiered?
[12:02] Liam O'Connor: Typically flat per-token for overage, but we can negotiate a tiered rate for committed usage in Dedicated contracts.
[12:11] Sara Patel: Ok thanks. That's helpful.
[12:15] [12:15] End of recording notes: rest of the call was follow-up scheduling, confirming who gets what docs.

Call ended 3:47 PM PT

Notes on transcription: a few product names got slightly misheard (e.g., K-V cache transcribed as K V cash), minor punctuation errors. Overall medium quality.
